<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 3 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 3 ==

== Biography ==

Ozma is the Ruler of Oz, referred to as "the girlish Ruler of Oz." She presides over her court from the palace, seating her guests — including Tiktok, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman — and directing state affairs. In one such gathering she calls a solemn conference to decide how to liberate the royal family of the Land of Ev from their long imprisonment, and she directly challenges the King's claim to have rightfully purchased that family as slaves, telling him plainly, "But that was wrong."

According to Dorothy's account, Ozma leads an expedition of Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, Billina, the Cowardly Lion, and the army of Oz to free the Queen of Ev and her ten children from the Nome King, traveling to his underground palace. There the Nome King challenges Ozma to identify the enchanted royal family among his ornaments within eleven guesses, or become an ornament herself. After the royal family's recovery and the crowning of Evardo Fifteenth as King of Ev, Dorothy accepts Ozma's invitation to return with her to the Land of Oz.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — friend. Their exchange in council — "We shall do it" — seems to reflect a shared resolve between the two, as Ozma keeps a chair at her own side for Dorothy during the conference on Ev.

'''[[Nome King]]''' — enemy. Ozma's flat rebuke of his claim that "the king can do no wrong" for enslaving the royal family of Ev — "But that was wrong" — suggests an adversarial relationship between them.

'''[[Tin Woodman]]''' — employment. He describes himself as acting on her command, "our gracious Ruler ordered me to assemble our army, which I did," indicating her authority over him.

'''[[Scarecrow]]''' — friend. He is seated near her council table at the palace, among those gathered around her for the conference on Ev, which seems to place him within her close circle.

'''[[King]]''' — enemy. The King who insists he lawfully purchased the royal family of Ev as slaves is met with Ozma's rebuke, "But that was wrong," pointing to an antagonistic relationship.

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* Ozma leads an expedition of Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, Billina, the Cowardly Lion, and an army of Oz to free the Queen of Ev and her ten children from the Nome King.
* The Nome King challenges Ozma to identify the enchanted royal family among his ornaments in eleven guesses, or become an ornament herself.
* Ozma fails all eleven guesses and is transformed into an emerald grasshopper; the Tin Woodman, the army officers, and Tiktok are also transformed after failing their own guesses.
* Ozma's party, including Dorothy, Tiktok, and Billina, crosses the desert on the magic carpet and travels to the Emerald City, meeting Jinjur (now a contented farm wife) along the way.
* Ozma is welcomed home with a grand reception, honors her officers and companions with gifts, and promotes the sole private, Omby Amby, to Captain General.
* Dorothy uses Ozma's magic picture to check on Aunt Em (well and content) and Uncle Henry (in Australia, sad and unwell) and decides she must return to him.
* Glinda advises that the magic belt only works within fairy countries, so Dorothy gives the belt to Ozma, who will use it to bring her back to Oz whenever she signals on a Saturday.

<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 4 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 4 ==

== Biography ==

Princess Ozma is the ruler of the Land of Oz. She presides in her court from a magnificent emerald throne, holding a jewelled sceptre and wearing a sparkling coronet, with the twenty-eight officers of her army and officials of the royal household standing behind her.

Ozma possesses the Nome King's Magic Belt and an enchanted picture through which she watches distant events. She has promised to look into the picture each day at four o'clock, and if she sees a certain sign, she will put on the Belt and wish the sender to be brought to her in Oz.

Ozma once brought the Sawhorse to life with a witch-powder, said to have been a boy at that time. After the Sawhorse won a race, she took the coronet from her own head and set it upon the horse, proclaiming him Prince of Horses and declaring that all other horses in the Land of Oz must thereafter be considered imitations of him.

When Dorothy reaches the palace, she is kept in Ozma's private rooms, and Jellia Jamb welcomes Zeb on Ozma's orders. Ozma also summons Eureka the kitten to speak with her directly, and later presides over a crowded public trial in the Throne Room, dressed in her most splendid robes of state.

== Narrative role ==

Princess Ozma rules from the Emerald City and keeps watch over the Land of Oz through her enchanted picture, which she consults every day at four o'clock. When Dorothy makes the agreed sign, Ozma puts on the Nome King's Magic Belt and wishes Dorothy, and then the rest of Dorothy's companions, to her side in the Emerald City.

Once the travelers arrive at the palace, a race is run between Jim and the Sawhorse. After the Sawhorse wins, injuring a leg and an ear in the contest, the Tin Woodman repairs the damage with a fresh limb cut from a tree. Ozma then takes the coronet from her own head and sets it upon the Sawhorse, proclaiming it Prince of Horses and declaring that, in the Land of Oz at least, every other horse must henceforth be considered a mere imitation of the Sawhorse.

Some time afterward, one of Ozma's white piglets disappears from her boudoir, and Dorothy's kitten Eureka is seen fleeing the room.

Ozma holds Eureka responsible for the piglet's disappearance, treating it as a killing, and orders the kitten imprisoned and brought to trial for murder before a jury of nine.

== Personality ==

Ozma shows herself as attentive and protective toward those she considers friends: she arranges to watch over Dorothy through an enchanted picture at a fixed hour each day, ready to invoke the Nome King's Magic Belt the moment a sign of distress appears. This routine suggests a ruler who takes personal responsibility for the safety of her companions rather than delegating it.

Her conduct at court reveals a gracious and ceremonious disposition. After the race between Jim and the Sawhorse, she publicly rewards the winner with her own coronet and a formal proclamation naming him "Prince of Horses," a gesture that shows generosity toward merit and a taste for solemn ritual. The same formality marks her appearance at the trial in the Throne Room, where she presides in her most splendid robes of state, sceptre and coronet in place, before a full court of officers and officials.

Ozma's interest in the Wizard, described as curiosity to meet a man of his renown, hints — though only tentatively — at an inquisitive streak toward figures of unusual reputation.

== Appearance ==

During the trial held in the Throne Room, Ozma appeared dressed in her most splendid robes of state, her jewelled sceptre in hand and a sparkling coronet upon her fair brow. This same coronet later left her own head when she placed it upon the Sawhorse's, honoring the wooden creature's victory in the race.

== Powers ==

Ozma keeps an enchanted picture in which she can watch distant events; each day at a fixed hour she looks into it to see whether anyone in need has made a sign calling for her help. She also holds the Nome King's Magic Belt, which she can put on to draw a person to her side in the Land of Oz at will. Her command of magic reaches back to a time when she was still a boy: using a witch-powder, she brought the Sawhorse to life.

== Relationships ==

'''[[DOROTHY]]''' — amitié. Ozma est désignée comme « mon amie la princesse Ozma », ce qui suggère un lien amical entre les deux.

'''[[Woggle-Bug]]''' — autorité. Lors du procès, c'est à un signal d'Ozma que le Woggle-Bug s'adresse au jury, ce qui pourrait indiquer une relation d'autorité de la princesse envers lui.

'''[[Zeb]]''' — attirance naissante. Le garçon aurait laissé échapper un soupir d'admiration en sa présence, ce qui pourrait suggérer un début d'attirance, sans certitude.

'''[[WIZARD]]''' — connaissance. Ozma se serait montrée curieuse de rencontrer le célèbre Magicien, ce qui suggère une relation de simple connaissance entre eux.

'''[[Sawhorse]]''' — amitié. Le Sawhorse évoque des aventures partagées avec Ozma et affirme qu'elle l'apprécie, ce qui indique une relation amicale entre eux.

== Trivia ==

* Ozma keeps an enchanted picture in which she can see distant places; by arrangement with Dorothy, she looks into it every day at four o'clock, and if Dorothy makes a certain sign, Ozma dons the Nome King's Magic Belt and wishes her back to the Land of Oz.
* According to an account given to Zeb, Ozma once brought the Sawhorse to life with a witch-powder "when she was a boy," a remark that left Zeb wondering aloud whether Ozma had once been male.
* During the Throne Room trial, Ozma presided in her most splendid robes of state, bearing a jewelled sceptre and a sparkling coronet, with twenty-eight officers of her army standing behind her throne.

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* At four o'clock Dorothy signals Ozma, who uses the Magic Belt to whisk her, then the rest of the group, to the Emerald City.
* Ozma crowns Sawhorse "Prince of Horses" and Tin Woodman repairs its leg and ear.
* Ozma's white piglet goes missing from her boudoir; Dorothy's kitten Eureka is seen fleeing the room.
* Ozma accuses Eureka and orders her imprisoned and put on trial for murder before a jury of nine.

<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 5 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 5 ==

== Biography ==

Ozma, also called Princess Ozma, rules the Emerald City and all four countries of Oz. Each of those countries has its own lesser ruler; by the shaggy man's account, confirmed by the boy at his side, these local rulers stand beneath Ozma much as officers stand beneath a general, with Ozma holding the highest position among them.

Ozma commands magic beyond her rank. She has brought Dorothy over to Oz on her Magic Carpet, one of the means, alongside the Nome King's Magic Belt, by which Dorothy has reached the Emerald City.

== Narrative role ==

Ozma's part in the story centers on her authority as ruler of Oz. The Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger meet the traveling party with Ozma's golden chariot and escort them into the Emerald City and into the royal palace. Later, Ozma's birthday celebration draws many guests to the palace and its grounds; once the festivities end, the [[Wizard]] sends several of the visitors home in magic bubbles, while Dorothy returns to Kansas by the Magic Belt.

== Personality ==

Ozma's authority is described as comprehensive yet layered: she "rules the Emerald City and all the four countries of Oz," while each country retains its own lesser ruler beneath her — an arrangement likened to an army, where "the little rulers are all captains, and Ozma's the general." This framing casts her as a sovereign who holds overall command without displacing the local governance beneath her, suggesting a disposition toward structured, delegated rule rather than direct micromanagement of every territory.

Consistent with this standing, she is said to have welcomed a visitor to Oz "in gracious accents" as "the girl Ruler" — a detail suggesting a courteous, dignified bearing toward those entering her domain, in keeping with her position as its foremost authority.

== Powers ==

Ozma commands magic beyond her own person: her Magic Carpet can carry a traveler across vast distances in an instant, as when it brought a companion back to the Emerald City after other magic had failed. Her authority extends over the Emerald City and all four countries of Oz, each governed by a lesser ruler who answers to her — as captains answer to a general.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — friend. Dorothy recalls that "Ozma took me over on her Magic Carpet," suggesting a bond of trust and assistance between the two.

'''[[Jellia Jamb]]''' — employment. Jellia Jamb is described as "Ozma's favorite attendant," which could indicate a relationship of service within Ozma's household.

'''[[Santa Claus]]''' — friend. An account holds that "Ozma invited me and I just couldn't help coming to celebrate the happy occasion," hinting at a friendly rapport extending an invitation from Ozma.

'''[[Jack Pumpkinhead]]''' — family. Jack Pumpkinhead states, "Ozma's my parent, you know, because she built my body and carved my pumpkin head," a claim that suggests a parental bond, though it rests on Jack Pumpkinhead's own framing of his creation.

'''[[THE shaggy man]]''' — acquaintance. Ozma greets him with "You are welcome to Oz," spoken "in gracious accents," suggesting a cordial but formal acquaintance befitting her position as ruler.

== Trivia ==

* Ozma once carried Dorothy across on her Magic Carpet, one of several magical means — alongside the Silver Shoes and the Nome King's Magic Belt — that have moved Dorothy between worlds.
* Although Ozma rules the Emerald City and all four countries of Oz, each country keeps its own smaller ruler; the shaggy man compares this arrangement to a military hierarchy, with the four rulers as captains and Ozma as the general.

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* The Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger meet the party with Ozma's golden chariot and escort them into the Emerald City and the royal palace.
* Ozma's birthday celebration draws many guests to the palace and grounds, and afterward the Wizard sends several visitors home in magic bubbles while Dorothy returns to Kansas by the Magic Belt.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 6 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 6 ==

== Biography ==

Ozma rules over all the countries of Oz, a wider authority than local rulers such as the Tin Woodman, who governs only the Winkie Country as its Emperor but answers to her. She has established what are known as the Defensive Settlements of Oz, including a town set aside for people who become Flutterbudgets, giving them a place entirely their own. She takes an interest in the excursions of her companions, having thought they might enjoy visiting the Fuddles and suggesting the trip to Fuddlecumjig. According to Dorothy, the Tin Woodman used to live with Ozma in the Emerald City before wanting a home of his own. According to the Tin Woodman's account, Ozma is said to have observed in her Magic Picture that the Nome King had dug a tunnel beneath the desert, seemingly planning an invasion of Oz alongside the Whimsies, Growleywogs, and Phanfasms.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — friend. Ozma appears to have arranged the day's outing, having "'vised" the group to see the Rigmaroles next, suggesting a familiar, guiding friendship between the two.

'''[[Roquat]]''' — enemy. Ozma once forced the old Nome King to liberate his captives, an act that casts her as Roquat's adversary.

'''[[Scarecrow]]''' — friend. Ozma gave him land of his own, and others helped him build his mansion there, suggesting a supportive friendship.

'''[[Uncle Henry]]''' — employment. Some connection between them seems to exist, though the excerpts do not detail its nature.

'''[[Glinda the Good]]''' — ally. The two seem to share some cooperative bond, though the excerpts do not specify how.

== References ==

<references/>

=== Events ===

* The Tin Woodman reveals Ozma saw in her Magic Picture that the Nome King dug a tunnel under the desert to invade Oz alongside the Whimsies, Growleywogs, and Phanfasms.
* The group visits the Scarecrow's new corn-shaped mansion and Jack Pumpkinhead's pumpkin farm; both agree to join them in the Emerald City to support Ozma.
* Ozma refuses to fight or flee, rejecting plans to arm the Winkies or escape to Kansas via the Magic Belt, choosing to share her people's fate.
* Ozma explains the Forbidden Fountain holds the Water of Oblivion, which erases all memory from anyone who drinks it.
* The Scarecrow's secret plan succeeds: dust in the tunnel makes the invading army thirsty, they drink from the Forbidden Fountain and forget their hostility, the resistant Nome King is thrown in too, and Ozma banishes the rest home with the Magic Belt.
</div>
